speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, and cognitive changes like forgetfulness and paranoia. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me when these symptoms first began and if they have been getting progressively worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the patient experienced any recent head injuries, fevers, or changes in his urinary habits, such as incontinence or difficulty initiating urination? Additionally, has he had any seizures or noticed any rhythmic jerking movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain
I need to visualize the brain structure to rule out a mass lesion or vascular event causing the focal weakness and cognitive decline.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the subacute progression of focal neurological deficits, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms alongside non-enhancing white matter lesions, we must rule out inflammatory or demyelinating conditions. Have you experienced any recent viral illnesses, unexplained weight loss, or night sweats in the past few months?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of untreated HIV and subacute cognitive decline with gait disturbances, we must rule out HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder or opportunistic infections. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Viral_Load_and_CD4_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HIV Viral Load: > 100,000 copies/mL; CD4+ Count: 56/μL

speaker: Doctor
text: With a CD4 count of 56 and high viral load, we must urgently rule out opportunistic infections like CMV or toxoplasmosis. REQUEST TEST: CSF_Analysis_and_Cultures

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CSF and non-enhancing MRI make opportunistic infections like toxoplasmosis or cryptococcosis unlikely, pointing toward HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder. I need to check for metabolic causes of encephalopathy and vitamin deficiencies common in advanced HIV. REQUEST TEST: Vitamin_B12_and_Folate_Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CSF and MRI findings, I suspect HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder rather than an opportunistic infection. To rule out other metabolic causes, REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Function_Tests

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal metabolic workup, non-enhancing white matter lesions, and severe immunosuppression, the clinical picture is classic for HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder
